messages.content: What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
When you launch a ball vertically upward with an initial speed of \(v_0 = 5\;\text{m·s}^{-1}\), its only force after leaving your hand (ignoring drag) is Earth's gravity pulling it downwards.  
In this idealized situation:

* **Acceleration** \(a = g \approx +9.81\;\text{m·s}^{-2}\) directed *toward Earth*.  

If you adopt the usual physics sign convention where “up” is positive, then the ball’s acceleration while moving upward is negative:

\[
a_{\text{ball}} = -\,g \approx -9.81\;\text{m·s}^{-2}.
\]

So regardless of how fast you throw it—whether 5 m/s, 20 m/s, or even 100 m/s—the magnitude of its acceleration remains essentially the same (≈ 9.8 m/s² toward the ground), because gravity acts uniformly on all objects near Earth’s surface.
